biological.citation: SARS-CoV-2-Induced PAPOLG Contributes to Inflammation Response by Stabilizing NF-κB mRNA. (PMID: 40607946)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was significantly upregulated in SARS-CoV-2-infected THP-1 macrophages. Knockdown of PAPOLG promoted NF-κB mRNA degradation and decreased TNF-α and IL-6 levels, while overexpression of PAPOLG stabilized NF-κB mRNA and enhanced cytokine expression. These results demonstrate that PAPOLG contributes to inflammatory responses by stabilizing NF-κB mRNA via alternative polyadenylation.

biological.citation: Systematic analysis of the frequently amplified 2p15-p16.1 locus reveals PAPOLG as a potential proto-oncogene in follicular and transformed follicular lymphoma. (PMID: 31410080)
biological.summary: Amplification of the 2p15-p16.1 locus is associated with increased transcription of PAPOLG in transformed follicular lymphoma (tFL), and PAPOLG expression increases after histological transformation from FL to tFL. Compared with normal B-cells, PAPOLG was significantly overexpressed in FL cases, while other genes in the locus (BCL11A, PUS10, USP34) did not show significant differences. These findings suggest PAPOLG may be the most critical gene in the 2p15-p16.1 amplicon for lymphoma transformation.

biological.citation: Comprehensive analysis of GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG axis in hepatocellular carcinoma. (PMID: 35482720)
biological.summary: Bioinformatics analysis identified PAPOLG as a component of the ceRNA network axis GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG in hepatocellular carcinoma, where PAPOLG is highly expressed and associated with poor prognosis. Immune infiltration analysis suggested this axis may affect macrophage polarization. A risk-prognosis model incorporating this axis predicted patient survival with AUC values of 0.691, 0.623, and 0.626 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively.

biological.citation: A diet rich in high-glucoraphanin broccoli interacts with genotype to reduce discordance in plasma metabolite profiles by modulating mitochondrial function. (PMID: 23964055)
biological.summary: SNPs associated with the PAPOLG gene were found to differentiate two discrete phenotypic responses to a high-glucoraphanin broccoli dietary intervention in a randomized controlled trial. PAPOLG genotype significantly affected plasma metabolic profiles including lipid and amino acid metabolites, TCA cycle intermediates, and acylcarnitines (p<0.001), and a significant PAPOLG genotype × diet interaction was observed (p<0.001). The HG broccoli diet reduced metabolic variation between the two PAPOLG genotype groups, consistent with rebalancing of mitochondrial metabolic reactions.
biological.sample_size: subjects in HG broccoli arm of a 12-week dietary intervention

biological.citation: A combined blood based gene expression and plasma protein abundance signature for diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer--a study of the OVCAD consortium. (PMID: 23551967)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified as one of 13 genes differentially expressed in leukocytes from epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) patients compared to controls. PAPOLG expression was included in a combined diagnostic model using gene expression and plasma protein biomarkers that achieved an AUC of 0.998 and a bootstrap-validated classification error of 2.8–3.1% for discriminating EOC patients from controls. This indicates PAPOLG is part of an immune response gene expression signature detectable in blood that is associated with EOC.
biological.sample_size: 343 samples (90 healthy, 6 cystadenoma, 8 low malignant potential tumor, 19 FIGO I/II, 220 FIGO III/IV EOC patients); validation: 65 controls and 224 EOC patients

biological.citation: Oocyte quality and in vivo embryo survival after ovarian stimulation in nulliparous and multiparous rabbit does. (PMID: 35724452)
biological.summary: PAPOL-G (PAPOLG) gene expression in rabbit oocytes was significantly different among experimental groups (nulliparous vs. multiparous, superovulated vs. control), indicating that both hyperstimulation treatment and reproductive history alter PAPOLG transcription in oocytes. PAPOLG was among only 4 of 11 analyzed genes (along with MATER, PAPOL-A, and ZAR-1) showing differential expression, suggesting a specific role in oocyte maturation and competence acquisition. These findings link PAPOLG expression to oocyte quality and in vivo embryo viability.

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Refining the 2p15-p16 Microdeletion Syndrome. (R. Lozano, W. Wilcox)
biological.summary: PAPOLG is located within the 2p15-p16.1 microdeletion region associated with a syndrome characterized by developmental delay, microcephaly, and dysmorphic features. In a patient with a 1.11 Mb deletion at 2p15-16.1, PAPOLG was among the deleted genes, though the critical region for the neurodevelopmental phenotype was refined to exclude PAPOLG and implicate other genes such as KIAA1841. This report contextualizes PAPOLG's genomic location but does not assign it a causative role in the syndrome.
biological.sample_size: 1 patient (sixth reported case of 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome)

biological.citation: Analysis of differentially expressed microRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid. (PMID: 35997417)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was identified as a predicted target gene of differentially expressed miRNAs (including bta-miR-196a, bta-miR-2285aj-5p, bta-miR-143, bta-miR-2433, bta-miR-2284f, and bta-miR-2368-3p) in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid to model Staphylococcus aureus-induced mastitis. Target gene enrichment analysis placed PAPOLG and co-targets in the MAPK signaling pathway, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer pathways. This suggests PAPOLG may be regulated by miRNAs during inflammatory responses in mammary epithelial cells.
